newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Indupa sells stake in Bahia Blanca to Dow Chem, YPF.
newsitem.headline: Indupa sells stake in Bahia Blanca to Dow Chem, YPF.

text.p: Argentina's Indupa SAIC said Friday it sold its remaining 5.5 percent stake in Petroquimica Bahia Blanca (PBB) for $20.8 million to U.S. firm Dow Chemical Co and local oil company YPF SA.

Indupa, which is controlled by Belgium's Solvay SA, and is the leading local producer of PVC and caustic soda, sold 70 percent of its stake in the petrochemical company to Dow and 30 percent to YPF, an Indupa spokesman told Reuters.
The deal was finalized Thursday. It became possible after a judge earlier this month lifted a bankruptcy protection order on Indupa.
With the acquisition, Dow and YPF increase their already controlling stake in PBB, Argentina's leading producer of ethylene, the raw material for polyethylene.
Indupa is owned 38.12 percent by Derivados Petroquimicos, a consortium in which Solvay holds 70 percent, Dow 21 percent and YPF nine percent.
Another 12.89 percent of Indupa is in the hands of Solvay's Argentine unit Solvay Quimica SA. Solvay controls directly or indirectly 51.1 percent of Indupa.
Dow became the main producer of high density polyethylene in Argentina after it bought the Polisur plant from IPAKO and the former Petropol plant from Indupa.
